fatal_errors: The proposed short-range-ordering mechanism conflicts with the target mechanism of vacancy-associated Shockley-partial nucleation and stacking-fault-mediated plasticity.
The intervention is changed from orientation-dependent tensile loading of an FCC single crystal to a compression-versus-tension comparison, so it does not reconstruct the relevant controlled regime.

The sole evidence concerns Al0.1CrCoFeNi, an Al- and Co-containing alloy with substantially different chemical-ordering tendencies, and cannot establish strain-induced ordering in equiatomic FeNiCrMn.

The hypothesis omits the key predictions of maximum yield stress along <-111>, negligible yield-rate sensitivity over 10^8–10^10 s^-1, increasing dislocation density and flow stress with rate, and absence of twinning or bulk phase transformation.
explanation: The response addresses temperature- and rate-dependent mechanics and provides an explicit baseline, boundary, and falsification rule, but it largely substitutes a different scientific problem. The hidden regime is molecular-dynamics tensile loading of an annealed, periodic FCC FeNiCrMn single crystal along three crystallographic directions at 10, 300, and 600 K and 10^8–10^10 s^-1. Its behavior is explained by thermally assisted dislocation nucleation, Shockley partial slip, and intrinsic/extrinsic stacking faults. The generated hypothesis instead invokes a compression-specific clustering-to-ordering transition over quasi-static through dynamic rates and temperatures extending beyond the target range. Its proposed paired compression/tension test is testable in principle, although ordinary diffraction has limited sensitivity to element-specific short-range order and atom-probe tomography is not ordinarily an in situ deformation measurement. Most importantly, E1 supports this phenomenon only in Al0.1CrCoFeNi at 10^10 s^-1; Al strongly changes ordering behavior, and the evidence does not validate transfer to Co-free equiatomic FeNiCrMn. Thus the proposal is novel and falsifiable but insufficiently supported and does not recover the target mechanism or outcomes.
